title: Hazel Crest Police hunt for men in viral gun video: 'We have already identified a few'
text:
Hazel Crest Police hunt for men in viral gun video: ‘We have already identified a few’
A disturbing Hazel Crest video circulating online showing self-identified gang members flashing what appear to be illegally modified guns in broad daylight while walking around areas of Hazel Crest has prompted a police investigation.
The Hazel Crest Police Department responded to a request for comment from South Cook News with a Community Notice stating that the video shows approximately 10 young men with firearms in the area of 170th Street and Bulger Avenue and that some of those depicted have already been identified.
“This correspondence is to inform our community that we are actively and aggressively working with various sources to identify the subjects in the video and to hold them accountable as much as possible, both legally and civilly,” Mitchell said. “We have already identified a few of the subjects and we are collectively working identify the others.”
Mitchelle appealed to residents who may recognize the individuals.
“These young men are someone’s kids, they are someone’s neighbor, they are someone’s family member, they are someone’s classmate. Someone knows who they are. It is during times like this when community policing truly matters. The police department cannot do this alone.”
Police said the video does not appear to represent a direct threat to the general public.
“While this video is very disturbing, there does not appear to be any direct threat to the general public. The investigation will be ongoing.”
Davis shared the Community Notice with South Cook News in response to a request for comment on the video, the investigation and the department’s planned response.
Davis did not return a phone call or directly answer questions about potential arrests or charges, efforts to identify those depicted using police records, additional patrols or surveillance, or whether the firearms appeared to be illegally modified or possessed.
The video was published by Onna Couch TV, a YouTube channel that features content involving young men and street and gang culture in the Chicago area, including video of gang shootings.The footage depicts multiple men carrying or displaying firearms as they walk through Hazel Crest.
In one portion of the video, several men appear to gather near a jungle gym at a public park with firearms visible. In another, the group appears to look toward a vehicle traveling on a roadway before members display their guns. At another point, members of the group wave firearms while singing along to a rap song. The young men are also shown waving around thousands of dollars in cash.
Men depicted in a viral Hazel Crest video walk along a hiking trail while displaying firearms. (X / Matt Robinson)
Matt Robinson, who posted the video on X on Aug. 24, characterized those in the video as gang members.
“Teenage gang members in Chicago suburb Hazel Crest IL doing a vlog posted outside flashing guns in broad daylight,” he said.
Throughout the video those shown repeatedly reference firearms, neighborhood affiliations, rivalries and violence, although portions of the dialogue are difficult to make out.
At one point, a speaker identifies the location as Hazel Crest.
“We on 168 right now, though, on blood. That's how this. Y'all know who he is, though. Yeah, yeah. B block on my brother. B block,” one of those depicted says.
The speakers also appear to encourage one another to display their firearms on camera.
“We got the rappers, we got the clappers on stage and we got clappas,” another man says in the video.
Another man then appears to make a general threat to those living in the area.
“Hey bros, you want to get in here poppin'? He say who y'all got outside, he ain't even gotta say his name or I might just... Just show him what you got on you. Come on, come on,” one of the young men says.
The video includes a discussion about whether the participants feel safe openly carrying firearms in the neighborhood.
“Without saying too much, do y'all feel safe out here?” the Onna Couch TV cameraman asks.
One of the men responds by describing how the group moves through the neighborhood.
“We know how to get through the trenches. We know how to get through the trenches,” he says.
Another speaker similarly describes the group staying together while moving through the area.
“You see, we ain't spreading it out, we in a bunch. This the easiest type right here,” he says.
Near the end of the video, one of the young men describes Hazel Crest and the movement of people into and out of the community.
“A lot of motherfucking, like when we was growing up around this shit, a lot a motherfuckin' like migrated towards this shit. Like, so it was a lot of motherfukers moving to Hazel Crest and moving out of Hazel Crest shit like that, but shit. Hazel Crest's faking on those motherfuckers. This shit ain't going to lie like this. This shit can get like that though. I ain't gonna lie. You got to be from the burbs to know what's, to know whats going on in the bubs,” he says.
The newly circulating footage comes amid previous concerns over social-media videos showing firearms in public areas of Hazel Crest.
In 2022, Hazel Crest police responded to a social-media video showing two young men displaying a rifle and handgun near a children's playground. Police warned residents at the time about videos showing firearms in the village.
The latest footage drew commentary from Royce White, a former NBA player who ran for the U.S. Senate in Minnesota in 2024 and 2026.
White said the video is evidence that leftists “served Black youth up as a sacrifice for their color revolution.”
“Definitely white supremacy, no? Racism is the problem, right? You know what I thought of as soon as I saw this… My son and all these commies or cuckservatives who use this bs 2 YEAR order, issued by a liberal Lindsay here in Minneapolis, to attack my character. The idea that slapping your kid upside the head or grabbing him by the collar for disrespect and bad behavior, is equal to abuse, is exactly how you get this,” White said.
summary: The Hazel Crest Police Department responded to a request for comment from South Cook News with a Community Notice stating that the video shows approximately 10 young men with firearms in the area of 170th Street and Bulger Avenue and that some of those depicted have already been identified. “This correspondence is to inform our community that we are actively and aggressively working with various sources to identify the subjects in the video and to hold them accountable as much as possible, both legally and civilly,” Mitchell said.
